abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) is widely used to capture and render real scenes. Compositing objects from one capture into another has applications in many domains, such as VFX, architecture and interior design, or marketing. However, extracting an object from a source scene and naively pasting it into a target scene will fail to produce realistic results due to the different lighting conditions between the two scenes. To address this problem, we introduce a diffusion model that harmonizes naively composited images with inconsistent lighting. The model is trained with a heterogeneous dataset of image pairs (inconsistent composite input, consistent output), combining synthetic, generated, and real data. Our complete 3D solution allows a user to extract an object from the source scene and composite it into the target scene. From this, the (inconsistent) views of the target scene with the composite object are rendered. Our diffusion model harmonizes each one of these views, which are finally consolidated in a 3DGS representation with a post-optimization step. Our method provides visually compelling results, making object transfer between 3DGS easy to use and significantly improving quality compared to previous methods.

abstract: Personalized stylization based on subject and style LoRA fusion has emerged as a practical approach for controllable image generation. However, existing methods still struggle to balance subject consistency, style fidelity, and visual preference alignment, and many of them rely on additional training. To address these issues, we propose Tri-LoRA, a preference-aware multi-LoRA composition framework that coordinates spectral fusion, layer-selective preference injection, and delayed temporal scheduling for personalized stylization. In the spectral domain, we develop a data-free parameter-space optimization strategy at the composition stage to alleviate feature interference during subject-style LoRA fusion, where redundant style-spectrum components are selectively suppressed through energy-based singular value truncation. For preference alignment, we further introduce a reusable DPO-guided residual branch and regulate its influence through layer-selective injection and delayed timestep scheduling. This design improves visual preference alignment while reducing disruption to subject structure and style formation. Experiments show that Tri-LoRA achieves a more stable trade-off among subject preservation, style expression, and visual preference alignment. Quantitative comparisons, qualitative results, and ablation studies demonstrate its competitiveness against existing LoRA fusion baselines.

abstract: Despite their superior visual fidelity, analytical multi-layered material models remain difficult to integrate into production pipelines due to heavy computational overhead and relative noise. We present the Neural Material Adapter (NMA), a framework that bridges the gap between high-fidelity material data and efficient rendering by mapping complex appearances into the parameter space of differentiable analytic BRDFs. Our approach is founded on the insight that directionally invariant parameters are fundamentally insufficient to capture the directional complexity of real-world light transport. We demonstrate that by allowing these parameters to vary freely with incident direction, we create a representation that defines an appearance gamut that not only overlaps with layered materials but also opens up regions physically unattainable by standard layered models. We use this expanded representation to fit high-fidelity isotropic appearances to a parametric Principled BRDF with directional parameter variation. By leveraging the strong inductive bias of differentiable analytic priors, we train a lightweight neural adapter that enables remarkably stable learning from sparse, noisy reference data. The resulting model is compact enough for efficient CPU-based inference without precomputation and exhibits powerful zero-shot generalization: once trained, NMA predicts view-dependent parameters for unseen layered material configurations and high-resolution textures. By decoupling complex directional appearance from heavy simulation, NMA enables a new class of expressive, high-fidelity materials that remain fully compatible with existing industry-standard rendering pipelines.

abstract: Within the CG animation production pipeline, the challenges artists tackle in Lighting can be immense. Even minor adjustments require re-rendering massive scenes with slow offline renderers; global illumination has to be sampled and complex shaders have to be evaluated, leading to iteration times of minutes to hours per frame. To accelerate this process, we introduce a novel neural render proxy (NRP) that enables differentiable relighting of static scenes with fixed camera and materials at interactive rates. Our main insight is the decoupling of traditional rendering into path sampling and emission computation. From a single, light-agnostic render pass, we collect light transport data in the form of path samples. This enables rapidly sampling lighting conditions on the fly, and training a scene-specific lightweight neural network that learns how light is transported from any scene location to any image pixel. This approach is compatible with non-differentiable production renderers, induces minimal memory requirements during inference, and scales only with resolution and the number of light sources and parameters, but independently of scene and appearance complexity. Our evaluation demonstrates interactive frame rates for relighting (∼30–60 Hz) while closely approximating the visual fidelity of ground-truth path tracing. In addition, the differentiable NRP enables fast, gradient-based inverse workflows, allowing artists to efficiently solve for lighting parameters from intuitive image-space edits or generative targets.

abstract: We present a method for generating orthogonal quadrilateral meshes subject to user-defined feature alignment and sizing constraints. The approach relies on computing integrable orthogonal frame fields, whose symmetries are implicitly represented using orthogonally decomposable (odeco) tensors. We extend the existing 2D odeco integrability formulation to the 3D setting, and define the useful energies in a finite element approach. Our frame fields are shear-free (orthogonal) by construction, and we provide terms to minimize area and/or angle distortion. The optimization naturally creates and places singularities to achieve integrability, obviating the need for user placement or greedy iterative methods. We validate the method on both smooth surfaces and feature-rich CAD models. Compared to previous works on integrable frame fields, we offer better performance in the presence of mesh sizing constraints and achieve lower distortion metrics.

abstract: We propose a novel methodology to model globally G1 geometry-conforming metamaterials using Generalized Bézier-based (GB) patches. Since every canonical tile is inscribed in a unit cube, we exploit its natural decomposition in octants and design multi-sided patches for each octant. The orthogonality constraints in each octant’s GB surface ensure global G1 continuity in the entire parametric domain and, under the assumption of a global smooth mapping that fills a desired free-form volume by deformed cubes, results in globally G1 metamaterial in physical space. The presented tiles can be graded in both shape and thickness using only a few shape parameters preserving their continuity properties, thus enabling optimization of novel metamaterials in various applications. Using isogeometric analysis tools we show that a G1 metamaterial results in a smoother stress field than a typical G0 tile used in state-of-the-art parametric approaches. We further show that our tile, given the continuity constraints, is lighter in terms of necessary control points than state-of-the-art parametric tiles and can approximate popular implicit tiles with sufficient accuracy. Finally, our pipeline is demonstrated in several design/analysis examples.

abstract: 3D anomaly detection has shown strong promise for industrial quality inspection. However, most existing methods rely on category-specific training, resulting in high computational and storage costs as well as limited cross-category generalization. Therefore, unified modeling is more attractive for practical deployment, especially in industrial scenarios where multiple product categories need to be inspected within the same pipeline. Nevertheless, unified modeling remains challenging, as it must jointly support cross-category shared representation learning and accurate normal pattern reconstruction. To this end, we propose UniGRe-3D, a unified geometric reconstruction framework for multi-category 3D anomaly detection. Specifically, to learn unified representations across different categories, we design a geometry encoder that incorporates positional embeddings, multi-scale feature interaction, and local-global feature interaction, thereby improving the discriminative ability of the learned features for geometric anomalies. To enhance normal pattern reconstruction, we further introduce a reconstruction decoder that employs position-guided decoding and hierarchical progressive reconstruction, thereby enabling more accurate localization of anomalous regions via reconstruction discrepancies. We conducted experiments on multiple datasets, in particular, UniGRe-3D surpasses prior unified methods by 6.9% in object-level AUROC and 4.0% in point-level AUROC on Anomaly-ShapeNet.

abstract: Given limited camera budgets, identifying informative views is essential for effectively reconstructing a radiance field to achieve high-quality novel view synthesis. These views should adaptively sample the radiance field based on the geometry and view-dependent appearance of the scene. Existing methods typically optimize views by selecting from a predefined camera set or adopting a greedy next-best-view strategy, limiting the flexibility and accuracy of the optimization. In this paper, we propose a novel continuous view optimization framework, called Camera Splatting, which enables joint optimization of multiple views. Our key idea is to represent each camera as a specialized 3D Gaussian, called camera splat, allowing for gradient-based optimization within a continuous camera parameter space. To evaluate view optimality, we introduce virtual cameras, called point cameras placed at sampled points in the scene, which render camera splats and provide feedback on their spatial positions and orientations. The resulting optimized views effectively capture the view-dependent appearance of the scene at the sampled points. Integrated into a Gaussian splatting pipeline, our approach can efficiently and simultaneously optimize a large number of views. Quantitative and qualitative evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of the views optimized by Camera Splatting for novel view synthesis under a limited camera budget.

abstract: Cage-based deformation is a convenient way to create 3D animations of high-resolution meshes by means of moving the vertices of a low-resolution control mesh, the cage. The resulting animation is a dynamic mesh, that is, a sequence of meshes with shared connectivity, which is controlled entirely by the corresponding dynamic cage. In this paper, we propose to invert this process and to approximate a given mesh sequence with a cage-based animation of the average mesh of that sequence. This process effectively decomposes the data into a static shape, represented by the average mesh, and the motion, given by a dynamic cage sequence. One key application of this representation is data compression. We use mean value coordinates for binding the mesh to the cage and publicly available state-of-the-art algorithms for computing the average mesh and for compressing static and dynamic meshes. Apart from the general idea of inverse cage-based animation, we describe a novel approach for automatically creating a motion-aware cage for the average mesh as well as a method for optimizing the latter. Compared to direct compression of the given dynamic mesh, our overall pipeline turns out to give better results at high compression rates, which are the most relevant in practice. Moreover, the decomposition into shape and motion enables the user to modify the input sequence by editing the average mesh and propagating the changes to the whole sequence using the dynamic cage.

abstract: Bijective correspondence is essential for texture and signal transfer, serving as a core benchmark for shape matching quality. Although the recently proposed Neural Adjoint Map (NAM) advances 3D shape correspondence by generalizing linear spectral alignment to nonlinear, network-parameterized functions, it is inherently unidirectional, failing to guarantee map bijectivity; on the other hand, existing spectral embedding alignment methods that promote bijectivity rely on the reciprocal property of low-dimensional functional maps, which we point out potentially introduces an isometric mapping prior and degrades accuracy under non-isometric scenarios. To address these issues, we propose the Bijective Neural Adjoint Map (BNAM), a novel framework that bridges bidirectional NAMs under a soft invertibility constraint to encourage mutual bijectivity. Additionally, we introduce an iterative upsampling pipeline to efficiently estimate BNAM. Our method promotes map bijectivity while preserving mapping accuracy across challenging scenarios, including near-/non-isometric meshes and unstructured point clouds.

abstract: Tall Cell grids are an efficient grid structure for large-scale liquid simulation, reducing pressure degrees of freedom by preserving high resolution only near the liquid surface. Recently, Quadtree Tall Cells extended this idea by introducing adaptive horizontal refinement, achieving further acceleration. However, when large portions of the liquid surface contain fine-scale details or high-frequency oscillations, extensive quadtree subdivision becomes necessary, significantly reducing the effectiveness of the approach. We present Extended Quadtree Tall Cells, a novel adaptive grid framework that introduces optical-layer thickness as an additional degree of freedom on top of Quadtree Tall Cells. By adaptively controlling both horizontal resolution and optical-layer thickness, the proposed method effectively reduces pressure degrees of freedom even in highly refined regions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method reduces computational cost compared with Quadtree Tall Cells while maintaining comparable visual quality, particularly in scenes with complex free-surface motion.

abstract: Autoregressive models have proven effective for triangular mesh generation by transforming it into predicting the next face, converting the non-differentiable connectivity prediction into a sequence of token predictions. However, generating quad-only meshes remains challenging because quad faces impose stricter topological constraints than triangles. The model must not only serialize quad faces into a valid token sequence, but also support unambiguous connectivity reconstruction during deserialization. To address this, we propose Q-MAGIC, a novel autoregressive model for quad mesh generation. We first introduce a tailored serialization scheme for quad meshes, which requires at least two new vertices for the next face and is less flexible than triangles due to strict wiring constraints. To meet these requirements and reduce serialization length, we propose a singularity-aware serialization that prioritizes wiring from singular points, leading to more coherent traversals. Additionally, we propose a circular relative offset tokenization that encodes geometry mainly via local relative offsets. Built upon this representation, an autoregressive Transformer learns the underlying distribution of quad meshes via next-token prediction, enabling effective quad mesh generation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Q-MAGIC produces more compact sequences while consistently improving geometric fidelity and mesh quality compared to state-of-the-art methods.

abstract: Hair reconstruction remains fundamentally challenging due to the filamentary nature of strands, strong self-occlusion, and the difficulty of recovering globally consistent 1D structure from multi-view observations. While multi-view cues provide complementary geometric evidence, existing approaches based on learned priors or implicit volumetric representations often struggle to generalize across diverse hairstyles or preserve fine directional detail. Learned methods can over-constrain global structure due to limited training diversity, while implicit orientation fields tend to collapse multi-modal strand orientations into locally averaged estimates, losing high-frequency directional variation in heavily occluded regions. We depart from these approaches by introducing a sparse hierarchical reconstruction framework based on an ambiguous structure tensor representation that encodes local orientation distributions without committing to explicit strand directions. Our key insight is that preserving directional ambiguity during reconstruction enables robust aggregation of multi-view evidence, postponing directional commitment until sufficient global information is available to enforce consistency. To reconstruct heavily occluded regions, we introduce a boundary-driven propagation strategy that transfers reliable surface structure into the interior through locally coherent helical continuation, enabling unobserved geometry to remain consistent with surrounding strand flow. We further introduce a consensus-based disambiguation mechanism that resolves tensor ambiguity and helical chirality into globally consistent strand growth directions, together with a cross-view orientation regularization stage that stabilizes early surface reconstruction into thin, strand-aligned structures. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method significantly improves strand-level fidelity and structural coherence on highly occluded, curly, and geometrically complex hairstyles.

abstract: While co-speech gesture synthesis has made significant progress in generating natural full-body motion from speech, a frequent setting where characters hold objects while speaking remains largely underexplored. The core challenge is that motion capture data cannot be collected at scale for every possible object, making few-shot adaptation a practical necessity. Yet a handful of samples is hard to exploit: conditioning on them as motion examples imposes only a soft prior, yielding intermittent object-aware behavior, while finetuning the full model on them either overfits and loses gesture diversity or fails to produce stable, prop-appropriate motion on the holding arm. To address this, we present PropGesture, a few-shot framework that adapts to a target prop using a small set of example clips synthesized by a video generation model. Our key design is to localize object adaptation to the prop-holding arm, preserving gesture diversity while introducing object-specific dynamics locally. Specifically, a phase-based arm motion generator, pretrained on large-scale gesture data and finetuned on the example clips, resolves the many-to-many speech–gesture ambiguity through phase sampling and retrieves arm motion via motion matching. This arm motion is then inpainted into a pretrained gesture flow matching model that synthesizes the remaining body from speech. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our method through both perceptual and quantitative comparisons against motion-example-based and finetuning-based baselines. Source code and dataset are available at our project page.

abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) have become a fundamental component of modern visual computing systems, yet their reliability often degrades on out-of-distribution (OOD) inputs, i.e., test images that deviate from the training distribution. Such deviations may arise from high-level semantic shifts, where images belong to unseen categories, or from image-level covariate shifts, such as noise, blur, illumination changes, and compression artifacts. Although covariate shifts often preserve the original class identity, they can substantially distort low-level visual statistics and alter model responses, making them difficult to detect with methods designed primarily for semantic novelty. This challenge becomes more severe when semantic and covariate shifts coexist, as they jointly affect different levels of visual abstraction. To address this issue, we propose AFDisc, a unified OOD detection framework that exploits the hierarchical representations of DNNs. AFDisc is motivated by the observation that shallow features are more sensitive to appearance variations, while deep features encode richer semantic information. Based on this complementarity, we introduce an attentive fusion module that adaptively integrates appearance-sensitive cues from shallow layers and semantic cues from deep layers into a unified representation for detecting diverse distribution shifts. We further construct auxiliary supervision signals through controlled appearance perturbations, enabling the model to better capture the spectrum of real-world visual degradations. Extensive experiments under semantic and covariate shift settings demonstrate AFDisc’s effectiveness and its superior performance over prior state-of-the-art methods.

abstract: Unsupervised 3D point clouds anomaly detection aims to identify and localize anomalous geometric regions only using normal training samples. Existing methods predominantly rely on feature matching and geometric reconstruction, or implicit shape modeling, where anomalies are indirectly identified through task-specific deviation measures, such as feature discrepancies, reconstruction errors, or geometric deviations. Different from previous works, in this paper, we propose a new flow-based framework (PCAD-Flow) for 3D point clouds anomaly detection, which directly evaluates the anomaly scores from the point clouds by utilizing point-wise features based on exact likelihood estimation. Specifically, PCAD-Flow employs conditional normalizing flows to learn invertible mappings from point-wise feature representations to a tractable latent distribution, allowing anomaly scores to be computed directly from negative log-likelihoods under the learned normal distribution. To further capture local geometric structure, we introduce a Progressive Local Conditioning (PLC) module that progressively aggregates neighborhood information and injects multi-stage contextual cues into the flow transformation. This context-aware density modeling enables the framework to effectively distinguish anomalous geometric patterns from normal local variations. Extensive experiments on Real3D-AD and Anomaly-ShapeNet demonstrate that PCAD-Flow achieves state-of-the-art performance on both object-level anomaly detection and point-level anomaly localization. Particularly, the proposed method obtains substantial improvements in localization accuracy than previous methods on the real-world point clouds benchmarks.

abstract: Skewed oriented bounding boxes (SOBBs) have recently been proposed as an alternative to the axis-aligned bounding boxes (AABBs) for the construction of bounding volume hierarchies (BVHs) for ray tracing. We expand this idea further and propose efficient algorithms for constructing compressed wide BVHs with SOBBs and updating these BVHs for dynamic scenes. The proposed approach typically yields between 1.07x and 1.6x faster traversal of secondary rays than the state-of-the-art compressed wide AABB BVH with extreme cases approaching 10x speedup. This is achieved at the cost of 1.15x slower build times and 7-15 bits of extra information per node. Our newly proposed refit algorithm for SOBB hierarchies is more than 3x faster than the original SOBB refit approach and requires roughly 4x less scratch memory. This makes it only about 1.45x slower compared to the refit of an equivalent wide AABB hierarchy while maintaining the faster performance profile of tighter bounding volumes. Together, these advances position SOBB hierarchies as a viable alternative for real-time ray tracing.

abstract: Feed-forward models such as VGGT recover camera poses and dense geometry in a single pass, and recent systems extend them into SLAM front-ends for long pinhole sequences. Panoramic video is an even more natural fit—one 360° view captures the full surround and needs no intrinsic calibration—yet no feed-forward SLAM system exists for it. We show that the crux is loop closure: well handled by pinhole pipelines, but uniquely hard on panoramas. Revisits are seen from arbitrary headings, where standard place descriptors, tied to viewing direction, fail; we therefore propose YIP, whose Fourier magnitude is exactly invariant to integer token-grid shifts and, up to discretization, approximately invariant to physical yaw. But this invariance cuts both ways: blind to heading, it also matches look-alike yet distant places, which an anchor-free backbone, with no sense of absolute position, aligns into false loops. The obvious defense is to verify each candidate’s geometry—our multi-signal verifier (MSV) does, rejecting many—but no per-candidate test is perfect, and across a flood of candidates these residual errors still admit enough false loops to corrupt the trajectory. Our key finding is that the cure is not a stronger verifier but an earlier one: candidate-stage suppression first collapses the flood, so that MSV—now judging only a handful—becomes decisive. This sparsify-then-verify order beats both verifying the full flood and gating loops after pose-graph optimization, when the trajectory is already corrupted. We call the resulting method PanoLoop. On 360Loc, it turns near-non-functional panoramic loop closure into an effective one, improving camera tracking over a strong panoramic visual-odometry baseline and producing globally consistent panoramic reconstructions.

abstract: Robotic manipulation of multi-state materials—cutting fruit, scooping ice cream, shoveling sand, splitting brittle solids—needs a simulator that handles large deformation, topology change, and two-way tool–material contact while staying fast enough to drive online reinforcement learning. We present MG-CD-MPM, a tool-centered localized extension of CD-MPM [WFL∗19] in which the implicit Ginzburg–Landau phase-field damage system is solved on a local patch by preconditioned conjugate gradients using a geometric-multigrid V-cycle as the preconditioner. The background MPM discretization remains uniform: only the damage solve is localized. Two-way rigid-tool coupling converts MPM contact impulses into forces and torques on the tool, exposing material resistance directly to the policy. The resulting Gym-like simulator covers soft solids, brittle materials, granular media, and viscoplastic or semi-fluid media within a unified per-particle constitutive layer, and we exercise it on six demonstrations: four cutting scenes spanning a soft-to-brittle stiffness/toughness spectrum (cut_jelly, cut_tofu, cut_wax, cut_peanut_brittle) plus scoop_icecream (viscoplastic) and shovel_sand (granular). We RL-train PPO agents (optionally warm-started from a behavior-cloning prior) on cut_tofu and cut_peanut_brittle as the closed-loop case studies; the remaining four demos exercise the same per-particle constitutive layer under scripted control.

abstract: Patch-based image vectorization methods usually represent image regions using fixed-sided patches, such as triangular or quadrilateral patches. However, such patches are often inefficient for irregular or semantically complex regions, as many small patches are required to approximate them accurately. To solve this problem, we propose an image vectorization method based on generalized Coons patches, representing an input image as a set of shape-adaptive polygonal patches. Compared with methods based on conventional Coons patches, our method can represent images with fewer patches and substantially alleviate foldover problems in irregular regions. To further improve the reconstruction accuracy inside each patch, an error-driven adaptive refinement mechanism is introduced. Interior control points are directly inserted at locations with large reconstruction errors, and their color attributes are determined through color fitting, without re-partitioning patches or modifying the patch topology. This mechanism is simple and flexible, and can progressively improve image reconstruction quality according to a prescribed error threshold. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves high-quality image reconstruction on various input images.

abstract: Gaussian Splatting has enabled real-time novel view synthesis, but its tightly coupled geometry and appearance representation often require a large number of primitives to reproduce high-frequency texture details, leading to substantial memory and optimization costs. Recent textured 2D Gaussian methods alleviate this limitation by attaching texture maps to Gaussian primitives. However, bridging the fundamental structural gap between discrete Gaussians and continuous 2D grids requires complex parameterizations that introduce severe computational overhead. This overhead fundamentally compromises the original efficiency of Gaussian Splatting, making the balance between detailed texturing and computational agility an unresolved challenge. To address these challenges, we propose LiteTex-GS, a fast and lightweight texturing framework for Gaussian Splatting. Our method initializes an extremely compact representation—assigning minimal local texture to each Gaussian and progressively allocates higher resolution only to primitives with significant reconstruction errors. To maintain a streamlined geometric scaffold, we introduce a contribution- and area-aware pruning strategy that eliminates low-utility Gaussians. Furthermore, to mitigate the gradient dilution caused by texture upsampling, we design a resolution-aware update rule that preserves rapid and stable convergence. Extensive experiments on standard novel view synthesis benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves competitive or superior rendering quality while using substantially fewer parameters and less training time than existing textured Gaussian baselines.

abstract: Bounding Volume Hierarchies (BVHs) are an integral part of modern real-time rendering and simulation systems. For animated geometry, however, the runtime cost of rebuilding the BVH every frame to match the deformed geometry is often prohibitive. State-of-the-art systems therefore amortize costs in several ways that negatively impact BVH quality: multi-level BVHs confine updates to dynamic geometry, fast builders are chosen among algorithms striking different balances between BVH build time and BVH quality, and the BVH topology is updated at a lower temporal frequency with most frames only refitting bounding volumes instead of rebuilding the entire hierarchy. In this work, we present a parametric BVH, which is able to represent parametric animations without an expensive BVH rebuild within the scarce frame budget, and without the usual quality degradation associated with a BVH refit. For this, we precompute a small set of BVH topologies that jointly cover the animation’s pose space with low error. At runtime, we obtain a BVH for the current pose by first selecting a BVH from the precomputed set, followed by a refit. We evaluate the practicality of our method on a large set of skeletal animations from the Mixamo dataset [Ado26]. Our approach matches results of high-quality BVH builders at the significantly lower runtime cost of a BVH refit. Compared to the common methodology of rebuilding the BVH each frame using a fast builder (e.g. LBVH), this equates to 1.25× lower SAH costs with 2.4× lower runtimes.

abstract: Phase unwrapping (PU) aims to recover continuous phase maps from wrapped measurements and is fundamental to graphics, depth sensing, holography, and remote sensing. However, accurate PU remains challenging due to noise, discontinuities, and severe wrapping ambiguities. In this paper, we propose MM-DPU, a memory-guided multi-constraint deep unfolding framework for robust phase unwrapping. The iterative optimization process is unfolded into a stage-wise reconstruction network, where each stage alternates between wrapped-gradient data consistency and learned phase-prior refinement. To improve error correction across stages, we introduce a dual residual memory mechanism that propagates the discrepancy between the data-consistent estimate and the phase-prior output. We further enhance the phase-prior network with a dual-branch bottleneck, combining lightweight global-context modeling and spatial-gated modulation to emphasize informative phase structures and suppress ambiguous wrapped patterns. The network is trained with a hybrid objective that integrates unsupervised wrapped-gradient fidelity and supervised phase-gradient constraints, jointly improving physical consistency and local structural accuracy. Experiments on PU for time-of-flight imaging, compressive holographic video, and Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar demonstrate the robustness and generalization ability of our method across diverse phase unwrapping scenarios.

abstract: Accurate head modeling requires a stable yet expressive geometric representation. Existing Gaussian-based head avatars commonly rely on parametric templates (e.g., FLAME) for Gaussian initialization and deformation, but these templates lack personalized priors and struggle to represent structures such as hair and clothing. To address this issue, we propose MGAvatar, a Gaussian–mesh hybrid representation that jointly models geometry and appearance through two Gaussian–mesh binding modes. Specifically, we introduce vertex-bound Gaussians and constrain their learnable parameters, enabling progressive mesh deformation to represent complex head geometry, while a pose-dependent offset module accounts for non-rigid deformations. Once geometry is stabilized, MGAvatar switches to face-bound Gaussians for appearance modeling. To improve appearance consistency across novel poses and viewpoints, we introduce a view-conditioned neural color field that alleviates artifacts caused by independently optimized Gaussian colors. In addition, we design a Gaussian offset network to predict Gaussian offset maps in the observation space, providing greater flexibility for face-bound Gaussians to capture dynamic facial textures. Extensive experiments on multi-view and monocular videos show that MGAvatar outperforms existing methods in rendering quality, producing high-fidelity head avatars with rich texture details.

abstract: Highly accurate 5-axis CNC machining requires a good, ideally higher order, match between the cutting tool and the reference surface along a common tangent direction. It has been shown that one can apply this, so-called curvature matching, even to convex surfaces using circular toroidal tools, by exploiting their interior hyperbolic points [BBR∗21]. However, such an approach typically requires a large tool and is very restrictive in terms of motion planning due to possible global collisions between the tool and the material block. In contrast, in this work we consider toroidal tools with non-convex inserts, which allow us to bring the hyperbolic points to the exterior side of the toroidal cutters, and therefore enable curvature-matched machining without requiring large tools or restricting tool movability. The proposed framework is compared against path- and motion-planning using classical circular tori on several benchmark geometries and demonstrates the superior behavior of cutting tools that have both elliptic and hyperbolic points on the cutting edge.

abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) remains challenging in dynamic outdoor scenes where dynamic distractors are coupled with large low-texture regions such as roads and walls. Binary mask-based foreground removal is insufficient—dynamic boundaries corrupt static optimization, while low-texture regions lack reliable matching cues. In our method, we propose Reliability-Aware Adaptive Gaussian Propagation (RAGP) for low-texture dynamic outdoor scenes. Our method adapts patch scales based on local structure and static reliability for pixel-level propagation, and fuses dynamic probability maps with rendering residuals into continuous reliability weights to constrain supervision, propagation filtering, and densification. Unlike foreground masking, RAGP converts dynamic priors into static reliability constraints and embeds them into geometric propagation. Experiments on dynamic outdoor benchmarks demonstrate that RAGP reduces artifacts and erroneous densification while improving low-texture reconstruction and rendering fidelity.

abstract: A surface representation suitable for geometry processing should be compact and explicit, provide global smoothness guarantees, support a wide range of surface topologies, and offer reliable access to differential quantities such as normals and surface energies, while remaining compatible with modern differentiable optimization. Yet existing neural representations typically sacrifice one or more of these properties: implicit fields typically require iso-surfacing for downstream use, while explicit neural maps are constrained by canonical-domain parametrizations and/or exhibit seam artifacts between local charts. We introduce Blended Chart Surfaces (BCS), a compact, network-free, explicit representation that is smooth by construction and anchored to user-provided topology. Given a coarse proxy mesh encoding the intended surface topology and approximate geometry, Blended Chart Surfaces jointly optimize for a polynomial map at each proxy vertex using an off-the-shelf optimizer to fit to an implicit target shape, avoiding the need for an input parametrization. Neighboring maps are fused using a smooth ‘one-ring coordinate’ blending scheme, decoupling surface topology and coarse geometry (carried by the proxy) from geometric details (carried by the smooth local patches). The resulting surface is globally smooth, fully differentiable, and enables stable evaluation of positions and derivatives, making differential quantities and surface energies directly accessible. Additionally, our construction is equivariant to rigid motions and scaling of the proxy mesh. We evaluate Blended Chart Surfaces on surfaces spanning varying topology and geometric complexity, and compare against explicit alternatives including interpolating-function baselines and mesh-displacement MLPs. Across these, Blended Chart Surfaces achieves a favorable trade-off among compactness, simplicity, access to differential quantities, and expressivity while remaining smooth across patch boundaries. Link to project webpage.

abstract: Multibody systems have widespread applications in diverse fields such as robotics, entertainment, and animation. Their capability to model and simulate intricate interactions among interconnected bodies makes them invaluable in various domains. However, complexity arises with factors like non-smooth contact handling, nonlinearity in flexible joints, and parallelization challenges. We introduce a stable and highly parallel GPU algorithm within affine body dynamics for solving constrained multibody dynamics with nonlinear constraints. Our innovation involves reformulating constrained multibody dynamics into a variational form, treating the system as a set of affine bodies connected with peridynamic bonds. This formulation provides a unified model for affine body dynamics, constraints, and contact within the peridynamics framework. It also facilitates the integration of the semi-implicit successive substitution method to solve nonlinear optimization in a global-local iterative manner. The proposed method obviates the necessity of assembling a global Hessian, rendering it highly suitable for efficient implementation on GPUs. This allows real-time simulation of intricate interactions involving both rigid and flexible bodies, encompassing contact, joint constraints, and friction.

abstract: Implicit neural representations (INRs) have been widely adopted for volume data modeling in scientific visualization due to their continuous representation capability and flexibility. However, existing INR-based methods still struggle to accurately capture high-frequency details due to spectral bias, which can degrade reconstruction quality and affect downstream analysis. To address this issue, we propose a frequency-decomposed residual learning framework for neural volume representation. Specifically, we decompose the volume data into low-frequency components and high-frequency residuals, and jointly model them with a shared INR by reformulating volume representation as a multi-task learning (MTL) problem. To alleviate potential learning conflicts between different frequency branches while preserving model compactness, we introduce a lightweight feature gating mechanism on top of the shared backbone to adaptively reweight shared features for the two branches, enabling more effective modeling of low- and high-frequency information. Experimental results on multiple scientific datasets demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms existing approaches in reconstruction, super-resolution, and compression tasks, while maintaining comparable model size and computational efficiency. Further ablation studies validate the effectiveness of the proposed frequency-decomposition and feature gating mechanism. Source code is publicly available at https://github.com/LiuLan2001/FDNR.

abstract: We describe a very simple algorithm to bijectively map between two simply-connected bounded planar domains given a set of n point correspondences constraining the homeomorphic boundary mapping. The bijective map Φ is the composition of two harmonic maps h1 and h2, which we call a double harmonic map. To compute Φ, we first map both domains to the unit disk using two conformal maps f1 and f2 and then determine a harmonic map g between the two disks that matches the boundary constraints. Composing f1 with g gives h1, and h2 is the inverse of f2. For the special case of n = 3, g is a Möbius transformation and Φ reduces to the classical conformal map. Our method allows a graceful tradeoff between conformality and harmonicity, and is efficient enough to be used in an interactive shape deformation system. All the maps involved are defined exclusively through their boundary maps and extended to piecewise linear maps with harmonic coordinates after triangulating the domains.

abstract: Palette-based localized recoloring is a common operation in texture-rich design workflows, such as textile recoloring, fashion colorway generation, interior surface editing, product material customization, and decorative pattern design. In these scenarios, users need to modify colors associated with selected palette components while preserving fine textures, printed structures, material details, soft transitions, and boundary appearance. Soft color segmentation provides a natural representation for this task by decomposing an image into palette-associated alpha layers. However, existing methods still face a trade-off among reconstruction fidelity, alpha-layer editability, and inference efficiency. Optimization-based and geometric methods can produce faithful decompositions but are often computationally expensive or mainly driven by color-space geometry, whereas learning-based methods are efficient but may lose high-frequency details and often do not explicitly model the relationship between image pixels and palette colors. We propose PASTEL, a palette-conditioned soft color segmentation framework for editable localized recoloring. PASTEL decomposes an image into normalized palette-associated alpha layers and residual-enhanced color layers. The core of PASTEL is a pixel–palette affinity learning formulation. Given an input image and its palette, we first encode image pixels and palette colors into a shared feature space through decoupled image–palette encoding. We then compute pixel–palette affinity scores and normalize them along the palette dimension to obtain interpretable alpha layers, where each layer is directly associated with a palette color. This design makes the decomposition consistent with palette-based compositing and suitable for localized recoloring. To preserve details beyond spatially constant palette colors, PASTEL introduces palette-constrained residual refinement: a lightweight predictor estimates layer-wise residual maps from the rough palette reconstruction and image-encoder features, and these residuals are attached to their corresponding palette maps before alpha compositing. The model is optimized with reconstruction, sparsity, and residual-distance objectives, keeping residual corrections tied to palette-associated layers. Experiments show that PASTEL achieves a favorable balance among reconstruction fidelity, localized editability, alpha-layer compactness, and inference efficiency, with palette retrieval serving as an additional application of the learned color representation.

abstract: In neural surface representation, how much does the presence of a geometric prior matter relative to its specific form or the network architecture? We study this question using the Neural Toroidal Patch (NTP), a representation built on the osculating torus, a local approximant that makes second-order contact with the target surface by matching position, normal, and both principal curvatures at each seed vertex. NTP decomposes a triangle mesh into toroidal patches by curvature-based fitting and iterative refinement; an MLP is then trained to predict only a small scalar residual along the torus normal, with the torus itself accounting for most of the local geometry. Holding the patch decomposition fixed and the training protocol uniform, no tested architectural augmentation improves over a flat three-layer MLP with 41K parameters, and a hierarchical design with 3.7× more parameters performs no better, scoring slightly but consistently lower across all five random seeds. An osculating torus, an osculating paraboloid, and a tangent plane reach comparable accuracy, within about 1.2× at supervised vertices and roughly 2× when the surface is queried continuously between vertices, so the specific form of the analytic base contributes less to final accuracy than its presence. In contrast, removing the base entirely, using a capacity-matched Direct MLP, is an order of magnitude worse; a control that keeps the analytic per-patch pose but removes the curved base surface remains substantially worse. The base also behaves as a data-efficient regularizer, its advantage over a base-free network widening as supervision thins and persisting when the base parameters are fit on the training vertices alone. The learned residual also transfers across shapes. A shared MLP trained on eight meshes adapts to four held-out meshes by tuning only per-patch latent codes, roughly halving their error, whereas a randomly initialized frozen baseline barely improves. For the smooth meshes studied here, the presence of an analytic base matters more than its specific form or the network architecture.

abstract: Generating dynamic 3D scenes with coherent geometry and motion from a text prompt or a single image, under user-specified camera trajectories, is a long-standing goal in computer graphics content creation. Existing pipelines cascade a video generator and a 4D reconstructor through an error-prone pose-estimation step, where estimation errors compound with generation artifacts. We present CamLoop4D, a generation-reconstruction co-design framework that closes this loop: a camera-conditioned video diffusion model and a 4D Gaussian reconstructor operate on the same Plücker trajectory tensor, removing pose re-estimation by construction, and the interface is generator-agnostic. For reconstruction, we introduce hybrid motion bases that combine six fixed se(3) generators encoding rigid-body priors with learnable non-rigid bases, reducing motion-bank storage from O(B · F) to O(B) while improving fidelity; under the matched-input protocol (all methods given the same real video and shared poses), the reconstruction module surpasses the strongest monocular baselines. CamLoop4D achieves the best PSNR/SSIM among all compared methods on the iPhone benchmark and the highest user-preference rates against seven recent baselines in text-to-4D and image-to-4D evaluation, and it generates an 80-frame 960×720 scene in ∼40 minutes on a single RTX 3090 with real-time 20 fps playback, bringing controllable 4D content creation within reach of individual creators. Our implementation is available at https://github.com/lihao1477024473/CamLoop4D.

abstract: Power diagrams with prescribed capacities are widely used in geometry processing, including blue-noise sampling, remeshing, and constrained clustering. The problem can be viewed as a semi-discrete optimal transport problem and is commonly discretized by dense sampling into a capacity-constrained assignment between n samples and m sites. Since this assignment is repeatedly solved in Lloyd-type optimization, its efficiency is crucial to scalability. We propose an exact algorithm for the resulting discrete capacity-constrained assignment problem. Unlike general-purpose minimum-cost flow solvers, which treat the input as an abstract graph, and entropic-regularized approximations, which sacrifice exactness, our method exploits the asymmetry m ≪ n between sites and samples, performing augmentations on a compressed auxiliary graph with only m + 2 nodes while maintaining point-level transfer costs using priority queues. We prove that augmenting paths in the full residual network can be projected to bounded-length walks on the auxiliary graph, yielding an O(nm² log n) running time and near-linear scaling in the number of samples for fixed m. Experiments on synthetic data and geometry-processing tasks show that our method achieves one or two orders of magnitude speedup over classical algorithms while preserving exact optimality for the discrete transport problem, enabling efficient computation of capacity-constrained power diagrams in large-scale sampled settings.

abstract: The Cosserat rod model captures the rich dynamics of slender structures yet is costly to simulate. Projective Dynamics (PD) accelerates simulation via a prefactorized system matrix but converges poorly under the extreme stretch-shear to bend-twist stiffness ratios of realistic materials, forcing practitioners to soften stiffness at the cost of visual artifacts. Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM)-based extensions handle this nonlinearity at the cost of local optimization overhead, yield limited acceleration, and exhibit perceptible damping under tight iteration budgets. In this paper, we propose an efficient and robust simulation framework based on a strain-based ADMM formulation. By defining auxiliary variables at the strain level and employing a two-level mathematical relaxation via Block Coordinate Descent and Projective Dynamics, our method recovers the fast, prefactorizable local-global architecture of classic PD while avoiding nonlinear local solves. We further augment the orientation block of the system matrix for bending-twisting constraints and introduce a robust penalty parameter clamping strategy. As a result, our method robustly simulates trees and hair under physically realistic parameters without per-scene tuning of the elastic penalty. Experiments show that our method converges faster than previous ADMM variants, reduces total runtime by 21% in a representative high stiffness ratio scenario, and exhibits less numerical damping than prior ADMM variants under tight iteration budgets.

abstract: Few-shot 3D point cloud semantic segmentation aims to segment novel categories in 3D scenes with scarce labeled support samples. Recent studies have predominantly followed the prototype-based paradigm, focusing mainly on prototype enhancement. However, they typically neglect the significance of feature representation, which is pivotal to segmentation accuracy. In this work, we propose a framework to explicitly refine 3D features by exploiting geometric dependencies and leveraging semantic knowledge from text. Specifically, we first introduce a Channel-Aware Feature Purification (CAFP) module, which mines latent global intra-channel correlations to purify 3D features for stronger discriminability. Secondly, we propose a Text-Anchored Modality Adaptation (TAMA) module to enhance inter-class separability and intra-class compactness of 3D features while alleviating the support-query gap under textual guidance. Within this module, class-specific text embeddings serve as semantic anchors to drive the adaptive alignment of features. Moreover, we design a Text-Geometry (TG) loss to further transfer inter-class semantic relationships from text to 3D geometry, facilitating more precise separations between foreground and background points. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superiority of our method, outperforming state-of-the-art approaches by margins of 5.69% and 9.66% in mIoU on S3DIS and ScanNet, respectively. Our code is available at: https://github.com/TZH716/TIFR.

abstract: Dense haze removal remains highly challenging due to severe information loss and heterogeneous degradation. Although recent diffusion-based methods have shown promising performance in image dehazing, they usually overlook the heterogeneous restoration difficulty induced by dense haze degradation, resulting in imbalanced optimization and unstable generation. To address these issues, we propose HeteroDiff, a novel heterogeneous diffusion framework for dense haze removal. Specifically, we exploit the heterogeneous degradation characteristics of dense haze images and devise an Interleaved Curriculum Learning (ICL) strategy that jointly schedules haze densities and diffusion timesteps, enabling the model to progressively learn restoration tasks from easy to hard for balanced optimization and accelerated convergence. Moreover, we incorporate depth priors into a Depth-Enhanced Noise Predictor (DENP) to improve structural restoration under severe haze degradation. During reverse diffusion sampling, a Context-Aware Sampling (CAS) strategy is further introduced to suppress hallucinated artifacts and improve spatial consistency by leveraging broader contextual information. Extensive experiments on NH-HAZE and DENSE-HAZE demonstrate that HeteroDiff consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in both visual quality and downstream object detection performance, particularly under severe haze conditions.

abstract: Disocclusion occurs when object movement reveals previously hidden content. Existing image-to-video methods provide different forms of motion and disocclusion control, yet the design space they span remains poorly understood. In this work, we systematically explore an algorithmic design space spanning motion specification (text-based versus tracking-based) and disocclusion specification (text-based versus image-based). To facilitate this study, we construct a benchmark consisting of both synthetic scenes and captured scenes, covering rigid and deformable motions, as well as static and dynamic disoccluded objects. We compare existing and adapted methods across this design space to analyze the strengths and limitations of different control strategies for handling disocclusions during motion. Our study reveals that tracking-based guidance improves motion accuracy, while image-based guidance improves the fidelity of newly revealed content. However, jointly controlling the appearance and dynamics of disoccluded objects remains a challenging open problem, particularly in scenarios where newly revealed objects undergo their own motion after becoming visible.

abstract: While 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) provides high-quality novel-view synthesis, its lack of an inherent hierarchy forces rasterization effort to scale with fine scene details rather than perceptually visible features. Existing Level of Detail (LoD) approaches typically address this by training discrete levels as independent models, relying on fixed selection thresholds that do not ensure smooth perceptual transitions. We introduce Hierarchical Level of Detail (HLoD) for 3DGS, a method that jointly optimizes Gaussian levels into a single, explicit parent-child hierarchy. To maintain a valid tree topology during adaptive density control, HLoD performs hierarchy-aware pruning and parent-child regularization, combined with scale safeguards to ensure spatial consistency across frequency bands. Unlike prior methods, HLoD avoids fixed size thresholds per level, preserving the ability to assign point density based on local geometric detail. At runtime, an efficient GPU traversal dynamically collapses fine sibling groups into their trained coarse parents based on local pixel-projection thresholds. Crucially, by integrating this traversal directly into the optimization process alongside strategies to balance photometric supervision between fine details and coarse nodes, HLoD maintains perceptually gradual LoD transitions that remain stable under inhomogeneous point distributions. Our evaluation demonstrates that HLoD achieves competitive reconstruction quality while enabling continuous control over the performance-quality trade-off along two axes: dynamically adjusting pixel-projection thresholds for spatially local LoD, and selectively rendering hierarchical subsets for adaptive memory scaling. Achieving these seamless transitions requires minimal traversal overhead while allowing overall performance to scale dynamically with scene complexity. Finally, we establish that joint optimization is structurally essential, as post-hoc hierarchical assignments fundamentally fail to preserve visual fidelity.

abstract: Recent extensions of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enable real-time novel view synthesis in dynamic scenes by learning time-conditioned Gaussian deformations. However, existing MLP-based methods typically estimate deformations independently at each timestamp, making them less robust to large or abrupt motions. To address this issue, we propose EvoGS, a 3DGS-based dynamic reconstruction framework that models Gaussian deformation as a temporal evolution process. EvoGS maintains persistent deformation states for each Gaussian, extrapolates future states from historical deformation states, and corrects the predictions with MLP-derived observations. The correction is adaptively weighted using a temporal residual memory and evolution statistics such as deformation velocity and trajectory deviation. To further improve reconstruction quality, EvoGS introduces deformation-aware densification. Clone and split operations are performed along corrected deformation directions, while an uncertainty-aware strategy suppresses densification for Gaussians with unstable deformation histories. Experiments show that EvoGS improves dynamic novel view synthesis quality and achieves competitive performance across benchmarks.

abstract: Maintaining visual contact with moving targets in complex three-dimensional environments is a fundamental challenge for aerial visual computing, as target visibility is jointly affected by scene geometry, dynamic motion, and viewpoint-dependent occlusions. Existing aerial vision-language navigation and tracking systems mainly focus on reaching static semantic goals or following non-adversarial moving targets. However, in realistic pursuit scenarios, targets may actively evade the UAV, exploit buildings, trees, vehicles, and other environmental structures, and perform strategic maneuvers to break line-of-sight. To address this challenge, we introduce Adversarial Dynamic Target Visual Navigation, a new task paradigm that formulates UAV pursuit as a visibility-aware viewpoint planning problem in dynamic 3D scenes. To support systematic evaluation, we construct FlySeek-Bench, a graphics-based benchmark featuring occlusion-rich 3D environments, language-conditioned target descriptions, rendered visual observations, and adversarial target policies that adapt to the UAV’s motion. We further propose FlySeek, a unified visibility-guided policy framework that combines predicted target hypotheses with semantic-geometric visibility and occlusion reasoning for preemptive viewpoint selection. By coupling these action-wise geometric priors with learned visual-language preferences, FlySeek improves target observability against active evasion before visual contact is lost. Extensive experiments in simulated and real-data-reconstructed scenes demonstrate that FlySeek improves tracking robustness, visibility continuity, and pursuit success compared with representative AVLN, tracking, and planning baselines, especially under severe occlusion and adversarial target motion. These results highlight the importance of moving beyond passive target following toward visibility-driven aerial pursuit in dynamic 3D environments. Code is available at https://github.com/JoshuaWenHIT/FlySeek.

abstract: Image diffusion models have shown impressive image generation capabilities but are often hard to control, in contrast to classical computer graphics pipelines such as physically based rendering. However, we observe that there is a bridge between light transport phenomena and the distribution of latent space values produced by such models. Thus, we introduce physically based rendering in the feature space learned by the variational autoencoders in generative models, enabling light transport simulation in the latent space. This allows us to leverage physically based rendering techniques to output latent maps for physically guided content generation. We propose modifications to the rendering equation, which, when paired with a differentiable renderer, can yield an optimal set of scene parameters that require only minimal refinement to accurately render into the pretrained latent space. We train our method on a single rendered image, and then demonstrate the generalization of the method to scene geometry changes, lighting changes, and camera view changes.

abstract: We present a method for constructing a simple quadrangulation of the sphere from an unordered set of n direction vectors, with application to parametric volumetric models of skeletal joints. We first select a quadrangulation encoding the joint topology by exhaustively enumerating candidate dual graphs, prioritizing convexity and regularity of the resulting quads. We then realize this topology on the sphere without crossings by solving a conflict-constrained assignment problem with lazy cyclic-order separation, and recover the corresponding primal graph. Experiments on direction sets from spherical Fibonacci sampling of size 3 to 20 show that the method robustly produces valid, high-quality quadrangulations across a range of input configurations. The resulting primal graph is directly converted into exact rational Bézier shell and column volumes, yielding a compact and precise volumetric representation of the joint. The approach extends naturally to multi-joint assemblies, enabling the construction of truss-based lattice structures within 3D domains.

abstract: Indoor 3D reconstruction can provide maps useful for robotic navigation. Current techniques, including truncated signed distance function (TSDF), neural radiance fields (NeRF), and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), have shown effectiveness in capturing the geometry and appearance of indoor scenes. However, these methods overlook panoptic reconstruction, limiting holistic indoor scene understanding. To this end, we propose a novel framework for comprehensive indoor 3D reconstruction using Gaussian representations, called OmniIndoor3D. This framework enables accurate appearance, geometry, and panoptic reconstruction of diverse indoor scenes captured by a consumer-level RGB-D camera. To compensate for the lack of geometric precision in vanilla 3DGS, OmniIndoor3D first combines multi-view RGB-D images into a coarse 3D reconstruction to initialize Gaussians and guide training. A lightweight MLP then decouples geometry from appearance as a spectral-bias-inspired smooth covariance regularizer. To improve the distribution of Gaussian primitives, we further propose a panoptic-guided densification strategy to encourage smoothness on planar surfaces. We perform thorough evaluations across multiple datasets and OmniIndoor3D achieves state-of-the-art performance in appearance, geometry, and panoptic reconstruction. Navigation evaluation is left for future work. The code will be released at: https://github.com/ucwxb/OmniIndoor3D.

abstract: Generating spatiotemporally consistent 4D content requires joint modeling of high-fidelity spatial details and realistic temporal dynamics. However, existing methods typically lack world knowledge learned from expansive 4D observations. As a result, generated scenes often struggle to maintain pose and temporal consistency in complex dynamic environments, leading to degraded generation quality. To address these challenges, we propose Dream4D, a novel 4D generation framework that integrates spatiotemporal priors from video generation with explicit sequential camera control. Our method adopts a three-stage pipeline. We first employ a vision–language model (VLM) to determine the camera trajectory that best captures the intended view from the input image and the instruction text. Next, a pose-conditioned diffusion model generates geometrically consistent image sequences along this trajectory. Finally, we use an advanced 4D generator to reconstruct a coherent and persistent 4D representation conditioned on the generated video. Dream4D jointly leverages the rich temporal priors of video diffusion models and the geometric awareness of reconstruction models to achieve high-quality image-to-4D generation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms existing methods in both pose and temporal consistency.

abstract: To solve PDE efficiently, posterior based standard Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR) techniques are widely used, but it requires a decent initial mesh for the first “cold start” computation. For steady-state elliptic PDEs on fixed curved surfaces with varying source terms or constraints, we propose a novel supervised learning method to infer a Riemannian metric field to guide the initial mesh generation. Without requiring knowledge of the solution, from the source term or constraints, our method is able to provide a high-quality “warm start” for AMR based on the “prior” learned from the dataset. Representing metric by tensor coefficients brings dependence of tangent bases and hinders the generality. Therefore, we encode the metric field using discrete edge lengths. Besides, we propose a solver-agnostic synthesis strategy to design a scalable dataset encoding the prior from pre-solved PDE instances. Our method demonstrates significant improvements on two common PDE problems: in Poisson problems, predicted metric-guided meshes reduce absolute discretization error by 27–43% relative to uniform meshes at matched resolution across our three test domains; in Obstacle problems, we achieve 2–3× faster convergence, confirming the benefit of integrating our “warm start” into existing AMR workflows.

abstract: Physics-based character control for high-dimensional humanoid motion requires reference motion-capture data to guide stable training of the reinforcement learning (RL) policy. However, the motion dynamics of the reference trajectory and the control target may differ in terms of mass, torque limits, and morphology. Conventional retargeting compensates for offsets based on kinematic structure, without considering real-world dynamics such as gravity, contact forces, and torque control, and the resulting motion fails to robustly guide policy training for the control target. We propose a motion refinement network that learns to automatically adjust retargeted results to be physically plausible, reflecting the non-linear relationship arising from the dynamic interplay between different skeleton structures and the environment. As the policy directly learns to track refined references in physical simulation, the resulting motions are free of physical artifacts, such as foot sliding, ground penetration, and implausible joint configurations, which are frequently observed in retargeting results applying inverse kinematics. While concurrent training of motion refinement and the RL policy often diverges, we introduce a warming-up scheme that initially trains the policy using only a fixed refinement network, then gradually introduces refinement offsets. The offsets are then selectively applied to the retargeted motion only when a substantial deviation is required. Experiments show that our method consistently improves physical plausibility over retargeting baselines using inverse kinematics, and further improves tracking performance particularly when combined with baselines that produce reasonably reliable initial references. Our method also generalizes robustly to retargeting across extremely different morphologies and physical properties, including dramatic changes in limb lengths and carrying of excessively heavy payloads.

abstract: Many procedural materials are implemented in legacy or production renderers where differentiable optimization is difficult to integrate, making black-box parameter fitting still relevant. In this setting, the optimizer receives only a scalar feedback value, so the objective function determines which visual cues are observable to the search. Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP) image matching is a strong baseline, but its global comparison can still underweight residual cues such as material color, feature scale, stripe spacing, gloss, or cellular structure. We propose Prompt-Conditioned Cue Matching, a target-relative CLIP response loss that uses a text prompt as a comparison axis between the target and candidate render. The prompt does not replace the target image; it specifies which cue should be compared more carefully. Because cue-only optimization is weakly anchored, we combine this term with CLIP image matching in an image-dominant hybrid loss. Experiments on checker, noise, wave, and Voronoi shaders, together with a real-capture verification, show that language-defined cue responses can provide targeted refinement when a visible residual cue remains.

abstract: Point cloud resampling aims to reduce redundancy while preserving geometric structures. However, practical inputs often pose challenges such as noise, incompleteness, and non-uniform distributions. These degraded conditions expose the limitations of existing methods, which cannot simultaneously ensure global coverage, regularity and feature preservation. In this paper, we propose WPDv2, a training-free and implicit-assisted Poisson-disk resampling framework that integrates implicit surface reconstruction with sharpness-aware feature weighting. It leverages implicit reconstruction to establish a coherent geometric domain and employs a winding number-guided sharpness field to drive density-adaptive sampling. Additionally, a feature-constrained Voronoi relaxation enhances spatial regularity while preserving distinct geometric structures with sharp features. Extensive experiments demonstrate that WPDv2 achieves superior feature preservation, robust performance under noisy and incomplete inputs. It provides a practical solution for high-fidelity point cloud resampling tasks.

abstract: City-scale scenes are increasingly prevalent in games and visualizations, making efficient rendering of mid- and far-range buildings crucial. It is desirable to have low-polygon-count proxies, connected bounding polygons derived from the originals. However, such proxies are still typically created manually, which is time and labor intensive. Architects frequently conceptualize the design as an assembly of primitives, known as building mass; for example, office buildings are often assembled with cuboids. Simultaneously, the volumetric faces and corner edges, known as architectural features, encode the physical boundaries and dominate the perceived shape. However, polygon simplification, point cloud reconstruction, and plane fitting primarily focus on local geometry while view-based clamping approximates the mass with selected silhouettes derived from geometric aspects. None considers architectural semantics resulting in failing to preserve architectural features and inducing perceptual distortion or excessive polygon counts. Therefore, we derive an automatic proxy construction framework from architectural semantics. Due to gravity, architects vertically align floors’ functional sectors and accessories, such as elevator/balcony shafts, to form the volumetric basis, denoted as roof-top volumes, of the building mass while each has its own separate top. In other words, the assembly of these roof-top volumes can be a good approximation. Thus, we identify functional sections via top-down ray casting and spatial segmentation with locations and orientations, fit their boundaries and heights with primitives, extrude them to form roof-top volumes and refine their sides laterally with a similar mechanism for mass approximation. Finally, quantitative comparisons against three baselines on 40 buildings under similar face budgets along with a 25-participant user study demonstrate that ours has higher perceptual fidelity, better feature preservation, and competitive efficiency.

abstract: Text-guided style editing of 3D assets is essential for adapting existing objects to diverse visual aesthetics in digital content creation. Despite rapid progress in 3D shape modeling, faithfully stylizing an existing asset remains challenging when the desired stylization involves fine-grained structural ornamentation, which requires the model to preserve the source geometry and object identity, while coherently integrating new style-specific details. We propose OrnaStyler, a zero-shot framework for text-guided ornament-aware 3D stylization. Built upon rectified flow-based generative modeling, OrnaStyler introduces an inversion-guided editing strategy that recovers content-aware latent representations at both geometry and appearance levels in a staged manner to facilitate faithful editing. Our core idea is to explicitly model the spatial configuration of stylistic elements, thereby mitigating the fundamental tension between content preservation and style expression in the voxel space. Specifically, at the geometry level, we manipulate voxel representations through flow inversion to synthesize ornament-enhanced structures while preserving the spatial identity of the source asset. Then, at the appearance level, we introduce an adjacency-aware feature inpainting mechanism to harmonize newly generated ornaments with the original content, yielding coherent geometry-appearance integration. Our approach operates solely in the inference phase and enables selective editing over geometric augmentation or appearance stylization. Extensive experiments on both generated and real-world 3D assets against prior methods demonstrate that OrnaStyler achieves state-of-the-art editing performance in terms of content preservation, style fidelity, and overall visual realism. Code is available at: https://github.com/tomohiro0427/OrnaStyler.

abstract: We present an angle-based metric optimization method for feature-aware quadrangulation. Unlike existing methods that optimize symmetric positive definite tensors directly, our approach uses triangle angles as the primary optimization variables. This choice has two immediate advantages. First, the constraints for local flatness (a necessary condition for local integrability), sharp features, and corners can be formulated linearly. Second, the positive orientation of the frame (a necessary condition for local injectivity) can be reduced to a simple box constraint on the angles. Moreover, the formulation naturally supports metric customization tasks, including sizing control, conformality, isometric regularization, and singularity specification. The final optimization problem consists of mostly convex terms and can be solved robustly and efficiently. Experiments on CAD models demonstrate improved frame-field integrability and greater parameterization robustness compared with existing approaches.

abstract: Training-free image editing with MMDiT-based flow models typically preserves source content by injecting source features into the target generation branch. However, achieving high-quality text-guided editing remains challenging because different editing tasks require different balances between content preservation and modification. To address this, we propose Function-Aware Regional Injection (FARI), a framework that analyzes the functional roles across MMDiT transformer blocks to determine where and how to inject source features. Through analysis, we identify four key functional components: (1) spatial anchoring blocks that preserve object positions and layout, (2) pre-activation blocks where editing-related semantic changes begin to emerge, (3) semantic blocks where editing-related semantic changes develop into explicit content modifications, and (4) late refinement blocks that consolidate visual information into a coherent final output. Based on these insights, FARI applies selective feature transfer in the anchoring and refinement blocks, while incorporating all source features in the pre-activation and semantic blocks to support larger content changes. This design enables interpretable control over preservation-modification trade-offs and provides editing policies tailored to different edit instructions (e.g., changing object, adjusting color). Experiments on a newly curated benchmark and PIE-Bench demonstrate that FARI achieves favorable trade-offs across all five edit instruction types by balancing preservation and editability, rather than relying on a single globally optimal injection policy.

abstract: Compact calligram generation aims to form a semantic shape while keeping letters recognizable. Most existing methods are shape-conditioned and mainly solve downstream letter layout inside a given contour. We study text-only calligram generation without an input contour. This setting is difficult because semantic shape formation and letter readability strongly interfere with each other when optimized in a single stage. Pushing the word toward a clear figure can easily damage glyph structure, while preserving readable letters can weaken the target shape. To address this difficulty, we present Telligram, a training-free, low-tuning, two-stage framework composed of Semantic Occupancy Prior Formation and Readability-Constrained Glyph Realization. The first stage uses Variational Score Distillation (VSD) with structured skeleton optimization and hierarchical gradient projection to produce a semantic occupancy prior. The second stage converts this occupancy prior into per-letter regions and reconstructs readable glyph layouts through lightweight geometric processing. The framework generates coherent and creative word-level semantic calligrams directly from text prompts.
